findings.title: In-flight lock Retry-After (BUSY_RETRY_AFTER_S) path has no test
findings.detail: status() computes `record.timestamps.length >= maxFailures ? Math.ceil((record.timestamps[0] + windowMs - t) / 1000) : BUSY_RETRY_AFTER_S`. Some 429s are caused by attempts still being verified, not by 5 counted failures. One input that reaches this: 8 concurrent wrong-password requests for alice (the LOGIN-003-AC9 scenario). When queued request 6 calls begin(), the limiter holds 2 timestamps and 3 pending attempts, so the request is locked and should get Retry-After 1. The AC9 test checks only status and body (`for (const res of locked) assert.equal(res.text, ...)`) and never reads the retry-after header. The only retry-after assertions are '60' and '30' in login-ratelimit.test.js (both the 5-timestamp path) and '1' on the 503 path. If the branch regressed, for example to `timestamps[0]` with empty or partial timestamps, the 429 would carry a wrong or 'NaN' Retry-After and no test would catch it. The current code is correct on inspection; this is a coverage gap only.
findings.location: src/login.js:74 (status(): retryAfter = ... : BUSY_RETRY_AFTER_S); test/login-concurrency.test.js 'concurrent guesses for one username stop at 5 verifications'

final_review.note:
Static review only. I ran no tests because the canonical file forbids running its proof and suite commands here, so every runtime check is NOT RUN. I read all of src/login.js, the src/server.js and src/users.js changes, README.md and the six new test files, and checked them against DEC-001 to DEC-012, INV-001 to INV-006 and LOGIN-001 to LOGIN-007. The checks I traced by hand all hold:
- Gate bound (4 running, 16 queued, synchronous null return) and FIFO order.
- Slot release in finally, including when a task throws synchronously.
- A queued attempt re-tests the lock with begin() at the start of its gate task, before has, verifyAsync or the dummy hash.
- In-flight attempts count toward the lock. By an ordering argument, no 60-second span can hold more than 5 counted failures for one username, except after eviction, which RISK-002 accepts.
- The 503 refusal changes no limiter state.
- Unknown usernames get the dummy hash, read from the users module object at call time.
- Limiter prune-then-evict in track(), used by both begin() and recordFailure().
- Session store eviction of the oldest token.
- Body cap and validation.
- No logging calls in src/login.js or src/users.js.
- The users.js changes are additive only.
Setup and cleanup both ran. The worktree was removed, and change.patch and inputs.json remain in /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/g/verify-3/final-review-opus.

compliance.note:
Opus-high fallback for the Codex spec-compliance trace. The setup block and the cleanup block both ran verbatim and succeeded. Cleanup removed the worktree and left /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/g/verify-3/compliance-opus empty. I changed no files. I ran no proof, suite or setup command from the canonical file, the views or the manifest.

Integrity checks (observed):
- execution-plan.json sha256 is 6b04649b..., which matches compile-identity.json and the manifest_sha256 of every frozen-run record.
- The canonical feature file sha256 is f5880a75..., which matches manifest source.sha256.
- The manifest lists 29 acceptance ids: 28 runtime and 1 static (LOGIN-006-AC3). The views mention exactly the same 29 ids.
- The acceptance ledger has 28 entries, one for each runtime id. For each one I checked that the record_sha256 matches its record file and that the log_sha256 in the record matches its log.
- Every record has: command equal to the manifest proof_command, cwd /srv/gp-v2/a3, head_before and head_after d004f807efbc39d004b3fe4352351c8dba3a9177, empty status_before and status_after, exit_code 0, timed_out false.
- Sample logs: login-ratelimit 9/9 pass, login-concurrency 7/7 pass, health+users 5/5 pass.

Trace of the code (src/login.js, src/server.js, src/users.js at d004f80) against the canonical acceptances and decisions:
- DEC-002 session store: crypto.randomBytes(32) base64url; at 10000 the oldest token is evicted (login.js:41-43).
- DEC-003 sliding-window limiter, counting attempts in flight:
  - Locked when timestamps.length + pending >= 5 (login.js:74).
  - Retry-After is ceil((oldest+60000-now)/1000) when 5 timestamps remain, otherwise BUSY_RETRY_AFTER_S (login.js:75).
  - check() never creates a record.
  - begin() and recordFailure() both go through track(), which first prunes expired idle records and then evicts the first-inserted record, keeping the 10000 bound (login.js:80-90).
- DEC-010 gate:
  - run() starts the task if running < maxActive, queues it if queue.length < maxQueued, and otherwise returns null.
  - The slot is released in finally, before the handler's result resolves, and the next task starts in FIFO order (login.js:129-149).
- Handler order:
  - readBody cap 4096: 413 with connection: close.
  - parseCredentials: 1..64 / 1..1024 strings, otherwise 400.
  - Arrival check(): 429.
  - gate.run, or 503 with retry-after 1 and the 401 body, with no limiter change.
  - Inside the task, begin() runs before users.has / verifyAsync / usersModule.hashPasswordAsync(password, DUMMY_SALT), which is read from the module object at call time.
  - end() runs on both paths; a rejection answers 500 and is not counted.
  - Success issues a token without touching the failure record (login.js:199-252).
- src/users.js only adds hashPasswordAsync (crypto.scrypt with KEY_LENGTH) and verifyAsync; the existing exports are unchanged.
- src/server.js routes only POST /login and adds the sessions/now/gate options. GET /health and the 404 fallback are unchanged.
- The only console call in src is the existing 'listening on' line (server.js:45).

I read each test against its acceptance's given/when/then:
- test/login-success: AC1-3 and 006-AC2.
- test/login-failure: 002-AC1/2.
- test/login-ratelimit: 003-AC1..8 and AC10, with the hashPasswordAsync spy installed before server.js is required.
- test/login-validation: 005-AC1..3.
- test/login-logging: 004-AC1/2, including the maxActive 0 / maxQueued 0 gate for the 503 path.
- test/login-concurrency: 003-AC9 and 007-AC1..6.

Each test asserts the exact statuses, bodies, headers, counters and gate states the canonical text names. For each test, the described isolated mutation would make an assertion fail or hit a 2-second waitFor deadline; I reasoned these through and did not run them. For example, under the active() <= maxActive mutation the maxPending assertion in 007-AC2 would see 5. I found no acceptance that is missing, implemented differently, or unproven.

LOGIN-006-AC3 (static): the six test files exist, and the package.json:9 test script glob "test/**/*.test.js" matches them.

Mutation negative controls were not part of this stage, and no frozen negative-control records were provided, so I did not verify them.
